scenarios.title: Keep long-option values intact
scenarios.summary: Parse a real long-option interface before publishing a lossless or counted report.
scenarios.objective: Accept required --source VALUE or --source=VALUE and --output VALUE or --output=VALUE, each exactly once in any order. Optional --count may repeat and selects physical line counting; otherwise preserve source bytes after the report header. A final -- is accepted only with no following operands. Unknown/extra arguments, missing values, empty values and repeated source/output print Invalid options on stderr with newline and exit2 before other checks. Then require distinct single-line names matching ASCII ^[a-z][a-z0-9._= -]{0,15}$: first lowercase letter, at most16 characters, then lowercase letters/digits/dot/underscore/equals/space/hyphen. Invalid names or equality print Invalid files, exit2. Missing source prints Missing source, exit1. Those failures preserve every file. After complete preflight replace OUTPUT with Source:NAME and Mode:full or Mode:count, each newline. Full mode appends source data exactly, including blank lines and missing final LF. Count mode adds Lines:N newline, counting each physical record including retained final non-LF text; empty data has0. Print Published:OUTPUT newline on stdout, empty stderr, exit0. Preserve all sources and unrelated files. Do not treat equals signs/spaces inside values as extra arguments or drop text after a second equals.

initial.source: # Write the complete script here. Each Run uses separate sample inputs and reset files.

cases.name: Full mode retains inline source spaces and equals at both name bounds
Inline output trailing LF cannot be removed before validation
Count handles blank and final nonLF rows with separate source and repeated flag
Source cannot be repeated
Output cannot be repeated
Later unknown option wins over an inline filename trailing LF
A separate option needs its value
Empty inline value wins over file lookup
Output must differ from source
Inline source trailing LF cannot become a different valid name
Missing named source is status one
Delimiter does not admit stray operands

solution:
bad_options() { printf 'Invalid options\n' >&2; exit 2; }
take_source() {
  if test "$seen_source" = yes; then bad_options; fi
  if test -z "$1"; then bad_options; fi
  source=$1
  seen_source=yes
}
take_output() {
  if test "$seen_output" = yes; then bad_options; fi
  if test -z "$1"; then bad_options; fi
  output=$1
  seen_output=yes
}
valid_name() {
  case "$1" in
    *'
'*) return 1 ;;
  esac
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -Eq -- '^[a-z][a-z0-9._= -]{0,15}$'
}
seen_source=no
seen_output=no
source=''
output=''
count=no
while test "$#" -gt 0; do
  case "$1" in
    --source=*) take_source "${1#--source=}"; shift ;;
    --output=*) take_output "${1#--output=}"; shift ;;
    --source)
      if test "$#" -lt 2; then bad_options; fi
      take_source "$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --output)
      if test "$#" -lt 2; then bad_options; fi
      take_output "$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --count) count=yes; shift ;;
    --)
      shift
      if test "$#" -ne 0; then bad_options; fi
      ;;
    *) bad_options ;;
  esac
done
if test "$seen_source" != yes || test "$seen_output" != yes; then bad_options; fi
if valid_name "$source" && valid_name "$output"; then :; else
  printf 'Invalid files\n' >&2
  exit 2
fi
if test "$source" = "$output"; then printf 'Invalid files\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if test -f "$source"; then :; else printf 'Missing source\n' >&2; exit 1; fi
printf 'Source:%s\nMode:%s\n' "$source" full > "$output"
if test "$count" = yes; then
  total=0
  while IFS= read -r line || test -n "$line"; do total=$((total+1)); done < "$source"
  printf 'Source:%s\nMode:count\nLines:%s\n' "$source" "$total" > "$output"
else
  cat -- "$source" >> "$output"
fi
printf 'Published:%s\n' "$output"
exit 0

teaching.prerequisite_note: Use the earlier lessons on getopts, quoted arguments, functions and status, line-by-line loops, arrays, and checking a complete plan before writing files. This unit introduces literal #/% removal in the simulator. It does not teach general Bash patterns.

concepts.title: One known prefix, once
concepts.text: ${tag#note=} removes one literal note= prefix when it matches. ${filename%.log} removes one literal .log suffix. A nonmatch leaves the whole value; neither form assigns back. #/% here do not mean general patterns, ##/%% or regular expressions.

concepts.title: Keep the rest as data
concepts.text: Removing --source= must preserve every following equals sign or space. Quote the result when assigning or calling a helper. A variable value is data and is not parsed as code again.

concepts.title: Consume one complete option
concepts.text: Loop while $# is greater than zero and inspect $1 with case. An inline --source=VALUE consumes one argument: remove the known prefix, then shift once. A separate --source VALUE needs at least two arguments before reading $2, then shift 2. Inspect the complete list before opening a file; a final -- has no operands in this interface.

concepts.title: Interface errors come first
concepts.text: Parse the complete argument list before reading or writing files. Track required options separately so duplicate and empty options cannot silently replace earlier values. --count is deliberately idempotent here.

concepts.title: Single line is not two valid lines
concepts.text: grep validates one line at a time. First reject LF anywhere in the whole filename: an active star on each side of a single-quoted literal line break makes a case pattern that also finds trailing LF. Do this before any cut command capture; then an anchored ASCII expression can enforce this task-specific name policy. This is not a general filesystem security model.

concepts.title: A supported alternative has its own premise
concepts.text: Command substitution removes trailing newline characters. Before using cut -d = -f 2- to capture an inline value, reject any newline in the original complete token. Only a single-line token reaches cut. Keep an invalid token as data for the later filename check, and finish parsing all options first so a later unknown or duplicate option still wins. With that premise enforced, -f 2- preserves every remaining equals field; -f 2 would discard later text. Never capture arbitrary file contents this way.

scenarios.title: Publish a collision-free normalized manifest
scenarios.summary: Plan a complete batch before copying exact file data or publishing its report.
scenarios.objective: Accept exactly MODE MANIFEST REPORT. MODE is preview or apply; wrong count/mode prints Usage: batch MODE MANIFEST REPORT newline on stderr and exits2 before file checks. MANIFEST/REPORT use the previous task’s single-line1–16-character ASCII name policy and must differ; failure prints Invalid files, exit2. Missing manifest prints Missing manifest, exit1. Read every physical line, including final non-LF text; count blank/comment lines in diagnostic line numbers. Skip empty lines and lines starting #. Every other line must be item=SOURCE, with SOURCE matching ^(incoming-)?[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,7}\.log$ exactly. Remove one .log suffix and one optional incoming- prefix to form BASE.copy. At each row, in this order: invalid key/value/shape prints Line N: invalid item (exit2); missing source prints Line N: missing source (exit1); any prior identical normalized destination prints Line N: duplicate destination (exit2); a destination equal to MANIFEST prints Line N: manifest collision (exit2); REPORT equal to that source or destination prints Line N: report collision (exit2). These checks run in both preview and apply, before any copying or report writes. Stop at the first row error and preserve ALL files, including earlier destinations and absent outputs. No whole-batch writing before this preflight. Preview prints each DEST=SOURCE newline then Count:N newline and changes no file, even REPORT. Apply copies exact source data to each planned destination, replaces REPORT with the same plan lines (empty for an empty plan), prints Published:N newline, empty stderr and exit0. Preserve the manifest, sources and unrelated files. This grades final contents and predictable preflight preservation, not atomic rename, concurrency or rollback after runtime/Stop.

initial.source: # Write the complete script here. Each Run uses separate sample inputs and reset files.

cases.name: Preview admits normalization and exact positive boundaries
Apply preserves complete data, empty files and final nonLF
An empty accepted plan publishes an empty report
Distinct source names can collide after normalization
Repeated source rows are not silently deduplicated
A later missing source preserves earlier destinations
Extra equals text is invalid, not a second field to discard
Malformed keys cannot be skipped after an earlier valid row
Manifest and report equality is rejected before reading
Report cannot be a normalized destination
Invalid mode takes priority over missing manifest
A late manifest destination collision preserves every earlier output

solution:
valid_name() {
  case "$1" in
    *'
'*) return 1 ;;
  esac
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -Eq -- '^[a-z][a-z0-9._= -]{0,15}$'
}
if test "$#" -ne 3; then printf 'Usage: batch MODE MANIFEST REPORT\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
mode=$1
manifest=$2
report=$3
case "$mode" in preview|apply) : ;; *) printf 'Usage: batch MODE MANIFEST REPORT\n' >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
if valid_name "$manifest" && valid_name "$report"; then :; else printf 'Invalid files\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if test "$manifest" = "$report"; then printf 'Invalid files\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if test -f "$manifest"; then :; else printf 'Missing manifest\n' >&2; exit 1; fi
items=()
destinations=()
plan=()
number=0
count=0
while IFS= read -r line || test -n "$line"; do
  number=$((number+1))
  case "$line" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; item=*) : ;; *) printf 'Line %s: invalid item\n' "$number" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
  item=${line#item=}
  if printf '%s\n' "$item" | grep -Eq -- '^(incoming-)?[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,7}\.log$'; then :; else
    printf 'Line %s: invalid item\n' "$number" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  stem=${item%.log}
  base=${stem#incoming-}
  destination=$base.copy
  if test -f "$item"; then :; else printf 'Line %s: missing source\n' "$number" >&2; exit 1; fi
  for previous in "${destinations[@]}"; do
    if test "$previous" = "$destination"; then printf 'Line %s: duplicate destination\n' "$number" >&2; exit 2; fi
  done
  if test "$destination" = "$manifest"; then printf 'Line %s: manifest collision\n' "$number" >&2; exit 2; fi
  if test "$report" = "$item" || test "$report" = "$destination"; then printf 'Line %s: report collision\n' "$number" >&2; exit 2; fi
  items=("${items[@]}" "$item")
  destinations=("${destinations[@]}" "$destination")
  plan=("${plan[@]}" "$destination=$item")
  count=$((count+1))
done < "$manifest"
if test "$mode" = preview; then
  for entry in "${plan[@]}"; do printf '%s\n' "$entry"; done
  printf 'Count:%s\n' "$count"
else
  for item in "${items[@]}"; do
    stem=${item%.log}
    base=${stem#incoming-}
    destination=$base.copy
    cat -- "$item" > "$destination"
  done
  printf '%s' '' > "$report"
  for entry in "${plan[@]}"; do printf '%s\n' "$entry" >> "$report"; done
  printf 'Published:%s\n' "$count"
fi
exit 0

teaching.prerequisite_note: Use the earlier lessons on getopts, quoted arguments, functions and status, line-by-line loops, arrays, and checking a complete plan before writing files. This unit introduces literal #/% removal in the simulator. It does not teach general Bash patterns.

concepts.title: A protocol value starts after its key
concepts.text: Check item= first, then ${line#item=} returns the entire remaining value. An extra equals sign remains and fails this filename policy; it must not be silently discarded.

concepts.title: Normalize exact edges
concepts.text: ${item%.log} removes just .log. ${stem#incoming-} removes just the optional prefix. incoming-a.log and a.log both normalize to a.copy, so source-name inequality does not prove destination uniqueness.

concepts.title: Plan before publishing
concepts.text: Validate every row, source existence, normalized duplicate, destination-versus-manifest collision and report collision before creating or truncating anything. A manifest can itself be named a.copy, so a normalized destination must be compared with the input manifest, not just other outputs. Apply the same preflight in preview and apply. Retain a bounded array plan with whole-array replacement: items=("${items[@]}" "$item"). += and computed indices are outside this simulator’s supported shell.

concepts.title: Copy file bytes, not captured output
concepts.text: Use cat with quoted source names for file data. $(cat ...) drops trailing newline characters, and echo can add one. Empty and non-LF files are real data cases.

concepts.title: State the limit honestly
concepts.text: Preflight protects against the stated predictable failures. This simulator does not provide atomic rename or a trap-based rollback transaction. Stop or a runtime resource failure can leave earlier simulated writes.
